reason: அத்தி is a traditional name of one of the ten nadis, but the only cited verse (1658) is given no breath reading and its அத்தி வரை is unconstrued, so no cited use supports the second sense.
The retained breath or seed as குளிகை is not a sense I can confirm as traditional; in 2305 the pill carries the poet to Sathuragiri along the sky path, and the inward reading is the proposer's (low).
Lotus and yogic centre are both traditional, and சிரமதிற் கமலம் in 1857 fairly names the crown lotus.

ய as the soul is traditional (Tirumanthiram 975), but the only cited use (1389, வட்டம்இட்ட யவ்வில்) is read as a yantra letter for fixing the breath, not as the soul; no cited verse uses the second sense.
Meru as the spinal axis is traditional, and மேரு நாடி in 1405 fairly names the spinal channel.
ம as malam or maya is the traditional pranava reading, and 1656 states it outright (மகார மாயை ... மலம்).
'Sky-channel' as a name for the central channel is not attested as a reading of விண்நாடி; it is a re-segmentation of 'seeking the sky' and the proposer's own reading is low.

Both senses are traditional, but neither cited use fairly carries the root-centre sense: in 1646 and 1863 (பர மூலநிலை) the source reading is the natural one, and the breath readings are low; the compounds where the centre is fixed are not cited.

கலை as a digit of the moon or phase of breath is traditional, but in 2302 (மறந்தெழு கலைமறந்தே) a list of things forgotten, arts or faculties reads as naturally, and the breath sense is low and unsupported by context.
Open space and the supreme space are both traditional, and பராபர வெளி (2298) and சுத்தப் பரவெளி (2300) fairly carry the second sense.
தாள் as foot and as door-bolt are both attested, and மூன்று தாள்திறந்து in 1404 fairly reads as the three knots; in 1393 கதவுதாள் is a plain bolt and the knot reading is stretched.
செப்பு as 'copper' is attested, but in 2314 செப்புக் குயமானார் does not construe as copper-workers with any confidence, and no other use is cited.
Fire raised from the root is a traditional sense, fairly carried by மூலநாடி தன்னில்வன்னி மூட்டி (1395) and மூலநாடியில் அனல்எழுப்பி (1405); in 1394 நீர்வன்னியை சமருவியே is too unclear to bear it.
Ganapati seated in the triangle of the root centre is a traditional placement, and திரிகோணக் குஞ்சரம் in 2293 fairly carries it.
பூரி as the in-breath is a guess from பூரகம்; in 1391 பூரியிட்ட தோத்திரம் is unclear and the reading is low, with no context fixing the breath.
Both senses of மாரணம் are attested, but 1650 only lists the word, and the reading itself says the verse makes no claim; nothing in it supports the calcination sense.

Rasa as mercury and as the taste of bliss are both traditional; in 2309 ரசபான போதை after the vision fairly reads as the drink of bliss (the second sense), though the mercury reading of it is stretched.
மெய் as truth and body are both standard; in 1645 விந்து நாதம் மெய்யாக வந்தது fairly allows 'came as the body', with the five elements as its seat. 1858's cited reading uses only 'truth'.
Eight as the numeral அ is a known Siddhar device, but in both cited verses the readings are low and the text gives no key, so the second sense is not fairly supported anywhere cited.

அ as first arising or as the soul is traditional, and அகாரம் இத்தனையும் ... எழுந்தது in 1655 states the first sense openly; in 1390 அவ்வில் read as the soul under the five-syllable key is stretched (that key makes ய the soul).
The nine as the body's openings is traditional; 2317 names ஒன்பது வாசல் and 301's நான்முழத்து ஒன்பது பீற்றத் துண்டம் fairly reads the same way.
தந்தி as a channel is given by the corpus gloss and fits 1404, where ஆன்றுதந்தி ஏறிடில் is followed by the nectar descending; the context supports the channel.
நடு as the central channel or brow point is traditional, and in 1409 நடுவறிந்து set against the root and crown (வேர், முடி) that Mal and Ayan sought outside is a fair, if low, yogic reading.
The three lights as sun, moon and fire, read as the two breaths and the root fire, is traditional, and in 2307 முச்சுடர் right after மூலாதாரந் fairly carries it.
The root channel identified with சுழுமுனை is traditional, and 1395, 1403, 1405 and 1413 all use it in a raising context that supports it; the two senses are close.
The sea as the heart is not a sense I can confirm as traditional for கடல், and நமதுகடலில் in 1397 looks like a misprint for நமதுடலில் (in our body).
Head and crown centre is a thin double reading but a traditional one, and சிரமதிற் கமலம் in 1857 carries it fairly.
The inner tirtha is a traditional Siddhar move, and ஆதி சக்கிரத்தினில் அமர்ந்துதீர்த்தம் ஆடுவன் in 1407 fairly puts the bath at a bodily centre.
Door and bodily opening are both traditional; 2317 (ஒன்பது வாசல்) and 1406 (மேலை வாசல்) fairly carry the second sense, while the three-knots reading of 1393's வாசல்மூன்று is low and stretched.

கவனம் is attested as speed or going (of a horse), and கமனம் as going is the traditional pill of flight, so 2305's கவனக் குளிகை fairly reads as a pill of flight; the double sense need not rest on emendation.
பெருவழி as the great path to the crown is traditional, and மேலாம் பெருவழி after the nine doors are shut in 2317 fairly carries it.
நீர் as the nectar is traditional in the fire-and-water pairing, and அந்த நீருண after kindling the root fire in 1395 fairly reads so; in 1394 நீர் may be the pronoun and the reading is stretched.
Foot and step (the four paths) are both plain senses, and the cited verses use each fairly: நாலுபாதம் in 1395, 1401 and 1646 as paths, பாதஞ் சத்தி in 1644 as foot.
Both senses of வாதம் are real, but the only cited verse (301) fixes the humour sense with பித்தம் and கோழை beside it, so no cited use supports alchemy.
Nectar and the yogic nectar of the crown are both traditional, and அமுதம்வந்து இறங்கிடும் after the ascent in 1404 fairly carries the second.
Emptiness and the void as the Supreme are both traditional, and 1860's சூனியமானத்தைச் சுட்டுவார் with the subtle intellect fairly makes it the goal.
The three mandalas of fire, sun and moon are a traditional Saiva reading, and மாறாத மண்டலம் ... மூன்று in 1651 fairly carries it; 1404's மண்டலம் உருவி is compatible.
Horse and breath are both traditional, and வாசிவானில் ஏறி (1396) and வாசியை நடத்திடில் (1397) fairly read as the breath practice.
சி as Siva is the traditional five-syllable reading, and 1656 (சிகார மூலம்) carries it fairly; 1390's சீயில் is a plausible further use.
